reviews.review:
Historically, it's one of the fathers of current rouge-likes. Game itself was created pretty well, but you can notice lack of experience from developers. However, they used it to create a great legacy for their title.

It's a classic, which is recommended but you must be aware it's an old school game and rouge-likes were still experimental genre.

In retrospect, and after putting loads of hours into both this and the second game, I can say that this one is certainly much better than the second, but still not worth investing all the hours I did into it.

On top of just having a more content than it's 3D counterpart (more enemies, more powerups), the levels are also much more interesting due to having a delicate mix of both platforming and combat, where-as in the second game most of the levels were pretty boring to traverse and even when some verticality was thrown in, it just wasn't enough to make them interesting to explore over and over again. 

I think what really makes this better than the second is that it doesn't feel like you're as much of a victim to the whims of malicious RNG. This game has so many exploits in the powerups which were nerfed in the sequel, you're much less likely to die randomly from a powerful enemy appearing out of view right behind you (except for that damn Overloading Magma Worm), and it's easy to find solid cheese strategies with most of the playable characters. 

That being said, this game's equivalent to the sequel blindsighting you all the time is that enemies tend to spawn so obnoxiously close to you that you are often immediately put into situations which are unwinnable, especially at the start of the game when you're desperately looking for any powerups. Where-as in the sequel I tend to die at any point in the play experience to something I couldn't have seen coming, here I usually die in the first few minutes to the first few enemies because accumulating powerups needed to take them on at the start is so insanely grindey that it borders on unplayable (as it can take hundreds of attacks to put down one enemy). That, or I get locked into a situation where hundreds of enemies accumulate in one place, so when I approach them I immediately die. 

This game has much better music and more fun gameplay than the sequel, but still isn't worth it when you realize that whether the play experience is good or awful or not is still ultimately completely out of your hands. It's addicting but still for the wrong reasons, and trying over and over again to trudge through an awful beginning just to simulate what a fun game like this might be like really isn't worth the headache. If this is what your typical rogue-like is like then count me out of that genre for good.
The game is quite simple, I don't mean easy, but mechanically there is not that much to it. Still really fun though
As close to perfection as possible.

This game is alright I suppose, there's not much to talk about really. The game is pretty old and feels outdated, the artstyle is really simple, the music is good (although it feels way to energetic for what's actually happening in-game), the gameplay is repetitive and kinda boring, enemies are dumb as bricks and their pathfinding can be really easily abused, there's basically no story to this game (at least I couldn't really pick up on one).

The achievements are pretty easy mostly because there's so few of them even though in-game there's a whole page for "challenges" that has quite a lot but the devs just cherry picked a handful for steam I guess.

4/10 If I could give it a thumbs sideways I would
